summary: Solves sketch groups made only of differences, values and midpoints through classes of offset parameters before their first solve. Differences join unknowns into classes, values and differences with fixed parameters pin them, a free class starts at the mean of its members less their offsets, and only classes a midpoint reads become columns, scaled so the smaller solve heads for the solution solving the whole group would: the one nearest the start. The group is then diagnosed whole, as before. Drags, groups with a distance, angle, tangency or other bent row, starts already polished, cycle or second-pin rows that do not hold exactly, rows left to solve that depend on others, and smaller solves or diagnoses that fall short are solved whole from their unchanged start, bit for bit as before. Against the 0.0.757 baseline module, 244 of 3,241 corpus and fuzz calls and 10 of 596 benchmark calls answer differently, each value within 4.7e-6 of its 1e-9 allowance and with the same status, diagnosis, freedom and labels. First solves of the four topology workloads take 0.37 to 0.44 of their time. The other 53 timed groups range from 0.96 to 1.18, within the host's noise: drags skip elimination, and the one at 1.18 measured 0.95 when timed again alone. Memory is unchanged. The module grows from 211,351 to 224,343 bytes, and the largest connected rectangle chain solved is still 83,333. Elimination in groups with bent rows can reach a different valid solution than the whole solve and is left as an open decision.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. Sketch groups held only by horizontal, vertical, coincident, equal radius, axis distance, fixed coordinate and midpoint relations can solve to slightly different values than 0.0.759, with other iteration counts; their status, diagnosis, freedom and named relations are unchanged. On the test corpus and benchmarks every value stayed within 4.7e-15 times the larger of 1 and the value. The solver stops within a tolerance that grows with the coordinates, so far from the origin the difference can be larger: 1.2e-7 mm for a sketch 1e9 mm away, where 0.0.760 lands on the exact solution.

checklist.schema: No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, CAD, storage, journal or worker reply change. The native module is rebuilt; its wire protocol stays 5. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation or input-version behavior change. WebMCP tools keep their arguments and result fields.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change and no new application controls.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change.
checklist.verification: Rust solver tests with twelve elimination tests, including 400 random sketches solved both ways (a 40,000-seed run agreed on all 11,386 sketches solved through classes), pins that hold only nearly, a repeated midpoint and a sketch 1e9 mm from the origin; solver:check; the baseline comparison against the 0.0.757 module with the elimination allowance applied per group; the A/B timing over 58 groups; the too-large boundary probe; the full Vitest suite, lint, ui:check, build and the release check.
